newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade to buy Serbia's 1997 wheat surplus.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade to buy Serbia's 1997 wheat surplus.

text.p: Serbia will buy up the entire market surplus of the 1997 wheat crop and pay for it in three instalments, the Belgrade daily Politika reported on Friday.
"The Serbian government decided to buy all market surpluses of the 1997 wheat crop," the paper quoted Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic as saying.
"Wheat will be paid in three instalments," he said.
The first instalment, 40 percent of the total price, will be paid in cash to farmers by the end of August.
The second and third instalments of 30 percent each will be paid in forward wheat contracts issued by Serbia's Commodity Reserve Agency by the end of September and the end of October.
Wheat can also be exchanged for fuel, fertiliser, seeds and agricultural equipment, Marjanovic said.
The Serbian government set the purchasing price of the 1997 wheat crop at 1.1 dinars per kilo.
Although the world wheat market has been in decline in the past year and the local ex-farm price is 0.60 dinars, the government decided to subsidise producers, Marjanovic said.
"We wanted to protect the interests of our farmers having in mind their enormous efforts and contribution to overall economic and social stability," Marjanovic said.
Serbia is expected to produce 2.749 million tonnes of a total of 2.8 million tonnes of wheat expected to be harvested in Yugoslavia this year on some 800,000 hectares.
The rest is to be produced in Montenegro.
The Serbian Chamber of Commerce has estimated the 1997 wheat market surplus at 1.6 million tonnes.
